pages.text: Green stems filled the potato patch on one side of the farm. Mom said, "Potatoes hide beneath the stems."
Pipo placed an empty basket in the middle of the patch. He would fill it.
Grandpa Sheep pointed his stick at a corner. "Have you dug over there? That is the real spot."
He dug in the corner with the tip of his stick. Only stones rolled out.
"Are they deeper?" The hole grew, but more stones came—stone, stone, stone.
Grandpa wiped sweat from his forehead. "In the old days, this was all potatoes."
The dug-up stones made a little tower. Grandpa plopped beside it. "A fine harvest of stones."
Pipo went to the green stems. He gently dug beneath them with both hands.
Potatoes came up in clusters! Big potatoes tumbled out.
The basket filled with potatoes. Grandpa quietly picked one up. He walked past the stone tower with his hands behind his back.
